articles.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.
points: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology.
The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).

articles.title: Patrice Désilets vows to make a sequel to Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey
articles.summary: Patrice Désilets, the creator of the Assassin's Creed series and director of 1666: Amsterdam, has said he will make a sequel to open-world human evolution survival game Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey.
body: Désilets, talking to me at a recent 1666: Amsterdam event, said 2019's Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey was written as a "volume one". "I've designed different volumes to eventually be growing the game," he said.
I didn't think he owned the Ancestors franchise - I thought Take-Two's defunct publishing label Private Division did. However, Désilets replied: "I own the IP. But it's complex."

So he could make a sequel if he wanted to. "Yeah," he confirmed. "I will. I will. And people can believe me because I'm ready to wait 16 fucking years to finish what I started [with 1666 Amsterdam]; I finish what I started."

Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey was an imaginative concept, a game that charted humankind's evolution from primate into upright walking human, across millions of years of time. As a player, you survived through different eras of third-person action survival gameplay, as the game lurched millions of years through time.

articles.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl meets The Finals in this wild new FPS
articles.summary: Like or Die is an upcoming FPS game from Korean developer NC, revealed for the first time during Gamescom 2026's Opening Night Live showcase. My first thought was that it looks a lot like Embark Studios' The Finals — from the environmental destruction and the abilities on show, such as zip lines…
body: Another similarity is that in The Finals, you're fighting in an arena on behalf of sponsors, with a colossal audience watching from afar. Meanwhile, the premise of Like or Die is that you're streaming your matches, with the goal of getting the most likes on a platform known as Quaya. Also watching the stream are potential sponsors. The more appreciation you get for your gameplay, the more gifts you may receive from these sponsors.

At Gamescom, I was shown a video of Like or Die behind closed doors. This delved deeper into the game's mechanics, but it notably ended with a zoom-out shot of a black hole in space. Of course, I had to ask about that, so I spoke with Kim Hwan, the head of IP at NC.

"In this alternate universe of Seoul, it's not just humans watching the stream," Hwan explained. "It's all kinds of creatures and aliens, and [the black hole] was the representation of the galaxy watching the stream. Space creatures are traveling and keeping an eye on the game."

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Zach Cregger Confirms He Already Has Sequels in Mind
articles.summary: Weapons director Zach Cregger is aiming for a very different approach with his new adaptation of Resident Evil. Rather than adapting the characters and narrative of Capcom's survival-horror game franchise, Cregger is instead translating what it feels like to exist in one of Resident Evil 's…
body: That may not sound like your typical franchise starter, but a sequel to Resident Evil is already looking likely.

Perhaps the most important indicator that Resident Evil will spawn a sequel is the movie's early box office performance. According to a report from Deadline, September's Resident Evil is already tracking toward a record-setting opening weekend for the franchise — somewhere between $35 million and $50 million domestically. Sony Pictures must be happy about that, considering the previous movie in the franchise, 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, finished its theatrical run with a $41.9 million worldwide haul.

Cregger himself might be on board for a sequel. He tells Polygon that he was thinking his Resident Evil journey would be a "one and done" flirtation with Capcom's IP. But after completing the film, he says he has more ideas for the franchise.
In an interview with Cregger, Polygon editor-in-chief Matt Patches asked the director if he was hoping to kickstart the franchise for a possible new trilogy.

articles.title: Valve has reportedly made £11bn from Steam already in 2026, and biggest earning new arrival is Forza Horizon 6
articles.summary: If you're Valve, 2026 has been a good year for the bank account, all thanks to the money Steam makes. According to new analysis, the PC storefront has made $15bn (~£11.10bn) already this year, representing Valve's cut from selling games, DLC and software on its platform.
body: So what was Steam's biggest revenue-generating new game release? That would be Forza Horizon 6, based on new Alinea Analytics data. The firm's analysis shows the open-world racing game has generated an estimated $210.5m (~£155.74m) in revenue for Valve.

Horizon 6 is followed closely by another major 2026 hit, Crimson Desert, itself having brought Valve $203.3m (~£150.42m) in revenue. Rounding out to the top three is Resident Evil Requiem, which made Valve $200.9m (~£148.64m) in revenue.

According to Alinea analyst Rhys Elliott, the top six highest-grossing new releases on Steam only amounted to just $1bn (~£735.8m) of that $15bn, or just 6.6 percent. Incidentally, two games in the top six - Crimson Desert and Meccha Chameleon - come from new intellectual properties (IPs).

Expanding the scope further to include the top 100 highest-grossing new releases in 2026, we see the value grows to $2.4bn (~£1.78bn) or a more respectable 15.9 percent of the store's overall revenue so far.

articles.title: Resident Evil's Zach Cregger: What Being 'Faithful' Really Means
articles.summary: Zach Cregger knows Resident Evil. The plots, yes, but also the panic. The dread of loading your last two bullets as you creep around a corner. The flailing terror of being ambushed and forgetting how to aim. Smashing buttons and running like hell to get a grip on what to do next.
body: “I'd rather watch a movie starring a schlub who's, like, out of shape and has never fired a gun before!” Cregger tells Polygon. “I wanna see that guy get chased through this gauntlet.”

September’s Resident Evil stars Austin Abrams ( Weapons ) as Bryan, a medical courier sent to Raccoon City to deliver an organ transplant. Terrible timing tbh — happening off to the side of Bryan’s hellish drive through whiteout conditions are the events of Resident Evil 2.

Unfortunately for Bryan, he is… nothing like Leon Kennedy. When things go catastrophically wrong, he squeals, stumbles, and struggles to click the safety off a pistol. I felt seen in a moment in which, to flee a snarling zombie lady, Bryan runs in circles around a turned-over cop car until he figures out how to attack back. Who among us would not yelp “shitshitshitshitshitshitshit” in that scenario, even behind the safety of a controller?

articles.title: 26 Years Later, the Best 'Dilbert' Quote Remains a Comic Strip Classic Despite Its Controversial Creator
articles.summary: Had he kept his mouth shut about his racist views for just a couple of years longer, we might never know how hate-filled the guy was, but I tend to think it’s good that he revealed his true nature before he died. Otherwise, the undeserving man would have been more celebrated when he passed.
body: To kick things off, let’s make clear that I think Scott Adams was a terrible person. After a successful career as the cartoonist behind Dilbert, the man blew his career up in the 2020s by revealing that he harbored disgusting views about people of color, specifically Black people. This resulted in immediate backlash and Dilbert was dropped from so many newspapers that Dilbert distributor Andrews McMeel Syndication dropped the comic too. In 2025, Adams announced he had Stage IV prostate cancer and he died in January 2026.

Recently, Polygon has been tracking down the best quotes and panels of some of the greatest comic strips of all time, including Calvin and Hobbes, Peanuts, and The Far Side. And while I still think Adams was an awful person, I wondered if it might be possible to track down the best Dilbert quote, too — a quote that spoke to why the comic was so successful, regardless of the man behind the strip — if such a thing is even possible.
points: Otherwise, the undeserving man would have been more celebrated when he passed.

articles.title: "This is super, super heavy" - Experts test Nvidia's divisive graphics-altering DLSS 5 tech and find it really does tank your game's frame-rate
articles.summary: Nvidia's gen-AI-powered, graphics-changing DLSS 5 tech has been tested and it really does take a heavy toll on a game's frame-rate. There was suspicion of this last week, ahead of DLSS 5's debut implementation in NBA 2K27, and now it's been properly tested, the performance toll has been confirmed.
body: Digital Foundry highlighted an approximately 40-60 percent frame-rate difference in NBA 2K27 when DLSS 5 was turned on. A topline GeForce RTX 5090 card running the game in Ultra settings at native 4K resolution dropped from 128.4 FPS to 62.7 FPS, for example. Even an RTX 5060 running Ultra settings in 1080p dropped from 72.8 FPS to 42.3 FPS.

"This is super, super heavy," Digital Foundry founder Richard Leadbetter said, "but it's also running on the entire RTX 50 series stack including laptops, which I didn't anticipate." And he added: "That's couched by the fact that, compared to a triple-A colossus, this is a relatively light game by comparison, so that has an impact."

The primary point of performance discussion was around "frame-time cost", which is a relatively fixed cost with DLSS 5, apparently. This varies from 8.2ms to 13.7ms depending on the graphics card and resolution being used. "Eight milliseconds of processing time at 4K on a 5090: that's mega expensive," Leadbetter said, "let's put it this way."
points: Nvidia's gen-AI-powered, graphics-changing DLSS 5 tech has been tested and it really does take a heavy toll on a game's frame-rate.

Schreier revealed this tidbit in a recent chat with former Polygon guides producer Ryan Gilliam, though without saying more besides. "I wouldn't count on this StarCraft game being a Destiny-like, I'll say that," said Schreier.

This was a particularly disappointing revelation for the host, who wanted another well-funded studio to carry Destiny's mantle. It is also notable that Blizzard, a developer of several mega-successful live service games, seemingly isn't making one in this instance - at least, from what we're working with here.

So if not Destiny-like, what recent game can the StarCraft project be compared to? Well, according to Windows Central editor Jez Corden, it may be a Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 -like and seemingly even takes cues from the Far Cry series.

articles.title: New horror game The Well Is Not Empty combines photophobic monsters with timer light switches and a lot of frenzied digging
articles.summary: "Never show the monster," horror film-makers, game-makers and other creepozoids have chanted, over the decades. The Well Is Not Empty wastes no time showing us the monster - one of the monsters, at least - and doesn't seem especially the worse for it. I mean, it's the worse, but in a good way.
body: Look, you can see the monster right there, hunkered up like a frightened puppy in the corner of the room. A scrawny little fellow with broken xylophone teeth and eyes that genuinely do make me think of the view from the bottom of a well. The monster is no threat, as long as you stay out of grabbing distance - and as long as the lights are on. The problem, as you've already guessed, is that the lights are unreliable. A lot of the ceiling bulbs in the open areas are set to a timer. Best make sure you're back behind the sturdy radiance of those construction lamps before the ticking runs out.

In The Well Is Not Empty, created by tweakEra with a demo on Steam as of writing, you're a villager sent to investigate why the water has run out. It turns out there's all kinds of shit down that well. Canteens. Offices. Expiring machines. Corpses clutching bloody letters. Some kind of huge prison complex, not entirely vacated. Balance beams over chasms. All of it brought to life in dingy, gangly, PSX-ified 3D.

articles.title: Riot MMO's future is 'incredibly bright' despite co-founder likening its development to the grail: 'Many a brave knight are going to die'
articles.summary: Despite a cloud of doom and gloom hanging over Riot's mysterious MMO in the wake of 2XKO's closure–including well-founded concerns from our own Harvey Randall —its co-founder seems confident in its ongoing development.
body: Marc Merrill dropped a mention of the MMO while answering a different question during the panel, which was immediately chased up by host Greg Miller with half-joking prompts for further morsels of information. Merrill mostly laughs it off, but does give a somewhat half-answer that at least indicates development of it is moving along at… some sort of pace. Though Merrill's description of creating an MMO makes it seem like it's giving Riot a bit of a hard time.

"We know what players' hopes and dreams are," he said. "And it's on us as a team—can we exceed in the execution, you know? But what a worthy quest. We jokingly call it 'the grail' internally because we're like 'Fuck it, you know, many a brave knight are going to die on the grail quest. But fuck it, it's the grail, so let's go.' That's the mindset that we really try to cultivate and that is incredibly hard to do at scale. But I think we're doing a reasonable job and I think the future's incredibly bright."

articles.title: Jensen Huang says 100,000 Nvidia GPUs were used to train OpenAI's latest model, GPT-6 Astra, and there's already plans to bring quadruple that amount of hardware online
articles.summary: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 Astra access to a limited number of organisations earlier this week, with wider subscriber access planned to soon follow. According to Jensen Huang via X, the model was trained on "~100K+ Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72" server racks, and there are already plans to…
body: Greg Brockman, the co-founder and president of OpenAI, told Stratechery that this was "the first run that we’ve trained on more than 100,000 GPUs." That's a staggering amount of hardware (and perhaps leaves little doubt as to how we ended up in a memory supply crisis ). But the thing that gives me more pause about Astra's announcement is the Nvidia CEO's assertion that "AGI has arrived."

To recap, 'Artificial General Intelligence' is used to broadly describe an AI model that either matches or surpasses human capability on complex cognitive tasks. Even Brockman admits that "People do have their own definition of AGI, it’s almost this blurry thing." Still, in that same interview he later goes on to add, "Maybe it was the previous model, maybe it’s Astra, maybe it’s the next model, but somewhere in there, I think we’re going to cross most people’s AGI threshold."
